newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends at fresh low with gasoline off high.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends at fresh low with gasoline off high.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed at the session low on Thursday, pushed down in late trade by a spurt of selling inspired by a slide in NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures from earlier highs.
Brokers said that with a lack a fundamental news, the market was taking all its cues from NYMEX contracts.
"As long as gasoline was holding up we were holding up, but it came off a bit and we had to fall into line with (NYMEX crude)," said one dealer.
April Brent closed 23 cents down at $19.32 a barrel. NYMEX crude and heating oil both ended weaker, with the latter pressured by forecasts of mild weather in the key market of the U.S. Northeast.

March unleaded gasoline ended 0.24 cents up at $62.50, but off the day's high of $63.00 cents a gallon. Gasoline's strength was mostly due to short covering in the prompt month ahead of the March expiry in refined products on Friday, U.S. dealers said.
"The unleaded was the only support today," said one IPE broker.

Markets on both sides of the Atlantic shrugged off news of the United Nations approval of a 40,000 barrel per day Iraqi crude sales contract with Indian Oil Corp. The 34th sales contract should put Iraq at the monetary cap of $1 billion for the first 90 day period of the U.N./Iraq oil-for-food deal, U.N. sources said on Thursday.
Iraq has already sold spot cargoes of crude in an effort to make up a shortfall in revenue under the U.N. deal caused by falling world oil prices.
Earlier, IPE March gas oil closed weaker after a session of choppy trade and thin volumes, dealers said.
"It was pretty featureless trade...we nudged up a bit, but then came off with heating oil under a bit of pressure," said one dealer.
March closed down $1.25 a tonne at $164.50 a tonne, having touched a high of $167.75.
